Based on DMCA anti-circumvention? That's an untested legal theory.

Yes, it's untested. However, it is absolutely clear that the DMCA makes it illegal to crack encryption schemes that protect media for the purpose of bypassing said encryption without clear permission to do so. It would take almost no effort whatsoever to bust the libdvdcss team if they were operating in the USA. Of course, they're not, so nobody is going to make the first step towards it. Even distributions stay out of the argument by just not including it in the first place.

FWIW, libdvdcss is not unlike (for example) typical PS2 modchips from back in the day (they contained no Sony code, only the ability to send "faulty" signals to the various security chips in the PS2 and 4 ASCII characters which Sony never laid claim to), and those have failed against the DMCA. In the libdvdcss version, we have a software specifically designed to test all key possibilities in a specific manner where a keymatch is guaranteed---just like the PS2 hack, no copyright infringement is involved and nobody's specific intellectual property (eg: specific leaked key) is involved. The only difference being that the PS2 hack also involved feeding four specific letters into the mechacon depending on what disc is being played. But those weren't a key anymore than PK^C^D is the "key" to a zip file. I also imagine there's file headers that libdvdcss has to react to as well (never bothered to get any deeper into it).

The obvious difference is that Sony mod chips were circumventing copy protection itself, while the most common use of vlc+css would be to simply play a movie.

Not to say that I know the outcome of the case, but it speaks volumes that Hollywood has so far not dared sue any Linux distributors for bundling libdvdcss.

One of the primarily advertised uses of mod chips was to allow playback of out-of-region games. And yes, it would also allow piracy.

One of the primarily advertised uses of libdvdcss is to play back movies, including out of region movies (assuming an RPC1 drive). It also allows piracy.

As for why linux distributors don't get sued, they are not being sued because they do not bundle libdvdcss. At a minimum, they do not bundle it in the USA, however, typically, they do not bundle it period.

A tip for those c++ programmers.

Local variables are allocated on the stack. But once in a while as a C++ developer you make a mistake when you move one byte too far.

Normally you should get an access violation, but if 2 memory local allocations are near each other you could corrupt the next variable and you get random errors. The trick is to swap the place of these variables, that could trigger the access violations or other bugs and discover your bug.

Another tip for C++ developers: Who frees the memory?.

The rule I always had was: The one that allocates it, must also free it. That way there is no discussion who should clean it up and have memory leaks.

If you do have to transport one memory structure to another location to process it, clone it! You take up more RAM for your application but your code will be more predictable and secure.

Honestly, things are in flux right now. With TGT expansion right around the corner, nobody is (or should be) crafting or disenchanting anything right now. This is because until we play with the new cards, we won't know how strong they are. We won't even know how good existing cards are!

Right now, I'd say don't craft or disenchant anything. If you still want to gain some sense of how good certain things are, perhaps this will help you. It's rather outdated though, so some parts of it won't quite be true any more.

http://www.hearthpwn.com/forums/hearthstone-general/card-discussion/5258-legendary-tier-crafting-guide

In general, I don't disenchant cards unless they are duplicates. As you get new cards, if you disenchant the duplicates, you'll start to build up dust. I don't usually craft new cards out of dust unless I'm specifically trying to complete a deck and need a card I don't have.

When you're just starting out, net decks, like the ones in the Trump Teachings videos are great for learning. You can find more online on various websites if you google it. As you get to know those more you'll start to feel more comfortable making substitutions in them. Some of those core decks like Frost Mage, Patron Warrior, Face Hunter, Zoolock, etc. are a good starting point and if you know those base decks, almost every other deck is a variation on those.
